title.value: 30×30 biodiversity gains rely on national coordination
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: 30×30 biodiversity gains rely on national coordination

extractions.description: This paper explores different 30x30 conservation scenarios in Canada, varying the dimension of biodiversity prioritized and the coordination approach (transnational, national, or regional), to identify decisions that influence our ability to capture biodiversity in spatial planning. It finds that a nationally coordinated approach to 30x30 could protect 65% of all species, representing 40% of all species-at-risk.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on biodiversity conservation and the effectiveness of different conservation strategies, which are central to sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Global commitments to protect 30% of land by 2030 present an opportunity to combat the biodiversity crisis

primary_category.justification: The paper directly addresses the protection of natural systems, specifically biodiversity, through conservation efforts.
primary_category.quote: Here, we explore a range of 30×30 con-servation scenarios that vary what dimension of biodiversity is prioritized

secondary_categories.justification: The study considers the impact of climate change on species distribution and incorporates climate refugia in the conservation planning.
secondary_categories.quote: Since effective spatial planning must incorporate climate change, we prioritized “win-win” areas within species’ current ranges that remain climatically viable into the future, thereby identifying climate refugia

primary_sub_category.justification: The primary focus is on biodiversity conservation, assessing how different conservation strategies affect the protection of various species and ecosystems.
primary_sub_category.quote: Using Canada as a model nation, we evaluate how well each scenario captures bio-diversity using scalable indicators while accounting for climate change, data bias, and uncertainty

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper uses climate models to predict future species ranges and identify climate-resilient areas for conservation.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Using Canada, a nation with considerable conservation potential and a rapidly changing climate, we quantify how well existing protected areas capture biodiversity, how much could be protected under 30 × 30, and test whether prioritizing different ele-ments of biodiversity versus coordinating protection at different spatial scales matters more for our ability to capture biodiversity in spatial planning.

new_primary_category.justification: None of the existing categories fit better than Natural Systems Protection.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: None of the existing subcategories fit better than Biodiversity.
